heading: Single-head ablations reveal partial compensation across model families on general text
definition: ablating single attention heads produces partial compensation on general text, across model families and sizes, not only on narrow tasks.
summary: The original study reports partial compensation across model families on general text, with layer summaries restricted to tokens where heads have the largest direct effects. An earlier study from the same group also reports head-level backup on general text; there is no independent reproduction.

suggested_status.by_scale: R1 at <1B, only if Iris counts arXiv:2310.04625's general-text result. This rests on the original plus that same-group paper's GPT-2 Small OpenWebText path ablation (L11H10 backing up L10H7). That paper predates the original. Its general-text result has no extracted row, and the paper has no V3 verdict. If Iris does not count it, <1B stays R0. R0 at 1-10B (original only). The original covers Pythia 160M, 410M and 1B, GPT-2 Small, Medium and Large, and Llama-7B; counts also put part of the study under 'not stated' size. No V3 test at toy, 10-100B or >100B (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size). Toy context, not a V3 test: in a different group's toy models, headwise zero ablation produces downstream compensation in target-token logit contribution under hierarchical training data, but near zero under flat data (d=1.82, p<0.001). The verdict placed this under fits-no-version, and the training data are synthetic, not general text (arXiv:2603.06592#f0, arXiv:2603.06592#r8, arXiv:2603.06592#r9). 1-10B and 10-100B context, not a V3 test: after a head is zeroed, oracle rescaling of another head recovers a fraction of output-KL damage (Raw Oracle metric) that rises from 0.2725 in Qwen2.5-1.5B to 0.4430 in Qwen2.5-14B. This is deliberately induced substitution, not spontaneous self-repair, and the study only cites self-repair (arXiv:2609.39259#f0, arXiv:2609.39259#r9, arXiv:2609.39259#r15; cites_only). No records above 100B.
suggested_status.reason: Only the original source is linked to V3 (counts: versions.V3.studies_tested = 1; versions.V3.original_sources_linked = [arXiv:2402.15390]). No other study has a V3 verdict or V3 rows (counts: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; versions.V3.verdicts supports, limits_scope and challenges each have studies = 0). The original shows partial head-level self-repair under resample ablation on The Pile, filtered to the top 2% of tokens, in base Pythia, GPT-2 and Llama-7B models (arXiv:2402.15390#R1-R7). All of this evidence is figure-only (counts: versions.V3.rows_by_evidence_form.figure_only = 7), with no controls and no uncertainty (counts: versions.V3.tested_with_controls = 0; versions.V3.tested_with_uncertainty = 0). Outside the V3 records, arXiv:2310.04625 (2023, so it predates the 2024 original) reports head-level backup on general text. It shares authors with an original (studies index: SAME GROUP), so it is the original group's R1 evidence, never an independent reproduction. In GPT-2 Small on OpenWebText, L11H10 backs up L10H7. Controlling the L10H7-to-L11H10 path explains up to half of L10H7's indirect loss effect, with little corresponding effect on KL divergence (Section 2.2, Appendix C, Figure 12). This result comes from a checker correction recorded in V5.support[4] and V5.method_sensitivity[5]; it has no extracted row and no V3 verdict. Its Appendix Q adds an unquantified observation in another checkpoint, Stanford GPT-2 Small E: after Name Mover ablation, a head wrote 'less against' the correct token. The record does not say on which text. That is one paper with several models, plus one earlier same-group result on a single head pair in GPT-2 Small, and no independent reproduction.
suggested_status.open_questions: These results would change the level: (1) an independent group (R2), or a same-author extension at 1B or above (R1 at that scale), reporting head-level self-repair on general text, ideally on another family (Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, OLMo), above 10B, or in instruct models; (2) a check of the studies the reader linked to V3 that the verdict did not count (counts: versions.V3.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not = 5), in case any has head-level results on general text; (3) results over unfiltered tokens, since the fraction depends on the top-2% filter and clipping; (4) a study finding no compensation for most heads on general text, which would move V3 toward C; (5) Iris's decision on whether arXiv:2310.04625's GPT-2 Small OpenWebText path-ablation result (Section 2.2, Appendix C, Figure 12) counts for V3. If it does, it needs extracted rows and a V3 verdict. If it does not, the level returns to R0.

source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

original_result.setup: They resample-ablated individual attention heads on The Pile, using 1 million tokens for Pythia-1B.
original_result.result: Partial compensation appeared across Pythia-160M, Pythia-410M, Pythia-1B, GPT2-Small, GPT2-Medium, GPT2-Large and Llama-7B. Layer summaries used the top 2% of tokens by head direct effect; exact compensation values were available only in figures.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Any study other than the original that tests head-level self-repair on general text, whether by the same authors or an independent group.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_tested = 1; versions.V3.original_sources_linked = [arXiv:2402.15390]; versions.V3.verdicts.supports/limits_scope/challenges each have studies = 0; versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0. counts: versions.V3.reader_said_tested_verdict_did_not = 5 (the reader linked these studies to V3 but the verdict did not count them as tests; they are not in this pack).

untested.what: Models above 10B parameters (the 10-100B and >100B buckets) and toy models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size lists only <1B, 1-10B and not stated. The largest V3 row is Llama-7B (arXiv:2402.15390#R7).

untested.what: Families other than Pythia, GPT-2 and Llama, such as Gemma, Qwen, Mistral and OLMo. These families appear in other versions' counts but not in V3's.
Post-trained (instruct/chat) models. All V3 rows are on pretraining models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_stage = {base: 1}; rows arXiv:2402.15390#R1-R7 give stage as pretraining model

untested.what: Compensation measured as task performance or over the full output distribution, rather than the correct-token logit.
untested.basis: 'problems' line in the pack header for arXiv:2402.15390: the main measure is correct next-token direct effect and logit change

wording_issues.phrase: on the full distribution / on general text
wording_issues.issue: Figure 1 summarizes tokens restricted to the top 2% by head direct effect. However, Section 2.2 and Figure 2 report Pythia-1B head direct effects and logit differences averaged across the whole one-million-token dataset; Appendix H provides analogous per-head plots for other models. General-text evidence is therefore not confined to filtered tokens. The outcome is centered correct-token logits, so 'full distribution' should not imply measurement of the full vocabulary distribution.

wording_issues.phrase: ablating single attention heads produces partial compensation
wording_issues.issue: The phrase can be read as covering any head. The original reports, anecdotally, that previous-token and induction heads do not seem to be self-repaired (Section 5.3.1; this is in no row). The pack header also says self-repair varies substantially by prompt and by head.

All V3 rows come from one paper. They cover three families, all pretraining models only: Pythia (160M, 410M, 1B), GPT-2 (Small, Medium, Large) and Llama (7B). Nothing above 7B is in the records (counts: versions.V3.studies_by_family, versions.V3.studies_by_size, versions.V3.studies_by_stage).

Compensation is measured as the gap between a head's direct effect and the change in correct next-token logit, not as task performance or the full output distribution (pack 'problems' line). R6's verdict fix says repair leaves a 'small, but noticeable' logit difference. No row gives an exact fraction.

method_sensitivity.what: Appendix A reports that filtering and clipping materially change the LayerNorm repair statistic: LayerNorm repair divided by clean head direct effect. Figure 10 gives the unfiltered, unclipped version. This sensitivity does not imply that all head-level results are filtered: Figure 1 uses the top 2% of tokens by head direct effect, while Section 2.2 and Figure 2 report Pythia-1B head direct effects and logit differences averaged across the whole one-million-token dataset. Appendix H provides analogous per-head plots for other models.

The pack header for the original says the LayerNorm contribution to self-repair depends on the ablation method. Although V3 rows R1–R7 use resample ablation, Section 3.2 tests individual Pythia-160M heads under mean, zero and resample ablation. Figure 4 reports LayerNorm ratios; Figure 5 compares direct effects with logit differences. Zero ablation can produce positive logit differences despite positive clean head direct effects. The Figure 5 caption names L11H0, while the prose names L11H10. This bears on V5/V6 as well as V3.

The pack header for the original says self-repair varies substantially by prompt and by head. The 'not in rows' line adds that previous-token and induction heads anecdotally do not seem to be self-repaired (Section 5.3.1).

status_amendment.public_note: A 2023 paper from the same research group as the original study found one attention head backing up another on ordinary web text in GPT-2 Small, so the suggested level rises from R0 (one paper) to R1 (extended by the same authors) for models under 1B parameters, if that paper is accepted as evidence. No independent group has reproduced the result yet; related toy-model and larger-model results are now mentioned as context only and do not change the level.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: R0 to R1. The R0 rested on 'no same-author or independent study tests it'. The checked V5 items record that arXiv:2310.04625 shows head-level backup on general text: L11H10 backs up L10H7 in GPT-2 Small on OpenWebText, explaining up to half of L10H7's indirect loss effect (Section 2.2, Appendix C, Figure 12). That study shares authors with an original, so by rule it is R1 evidence, not an independent reproduction. It applies at <1B only, to one head pair in one model, and it predates the original. The general-text result has no extracted row and the study has no V3 verdict, so the R1 depends on Iris counting it. If she does not, the level returns to R0. The toy and Qwen2.5 results added to by_scale are context only and do not affect the level.
